title: Common Schema Definitions
description: Shared definitions used across Vrooli service schemas

evidence.pattern: (?i)(no implementation|not applicable on this host os|no .* implementation)
(?i)(no implementation for the .* host mechanism|not applicable on this host os)

invariant.description: An OS-neutral relationship that must hold for a host capability to work. An invariant names no package and no package manager; platform providers derive concrete implementation details.

invariantApplicability.description: Optional host predicates for an invariant. An empty object means the invariant is always applicable.

duration.description: Duration with unit (ms, s, m, h, d)

verificationCheck.description: One-shot post-action verification probe. Used after installing a host tool or applying a host safeguard to confirm the action took effect. Distinct from runtime health monitoring (which runs continuously on an interval): a verificationCheck runs once and answers 'did the install or apply succeed?'.

command.description: Command to run for the verification.

files.description: Files that must exist for the verification to pass. Combined with `command`: file checks run first, then the command.

durableDataEntry.description: One durable on-disk location worth preserving. The single shared shape for both the operator runtime home (repo-contract.schema.json#/properties/runtime_home/properties/entries) and a resource's declared host state (resource.schema.json#/properties/durable_data/properties/entries). `regenerable` is the include/exclude switch: false = irreplaceable state that must be backed up; true = reconstructable (caches, logs, build output) and skipped.

path.description: Slash-normalized path of this entry, relative to its container's base (the runtime home, or a resource durable_data base). No backslashes. Leading slashes, drive letters, and parent traversal are enforced by repo-contract/resource validators rather than this portable JSON Schema regex.

kind.description: Whether this entry is a directory or a single file.

regenerable.description: True if the data here can be reconstructed (caches, logs, build output) and need not be backed up; false if it is durable state that must be preserved.

format.description: On-disk format hint for file entries (e.g. sqlite → capture a consistent database copy).

sensitive.description: True if the entry holds secrets/credentials (e.g. OAuth tokens). Surfaced with a warning and never auto-accepted; contents are never read into UIs or logs.

owner.description: Named authority responsible for writes, repair, and lifecycle decisions.

protected.description: True when the entry is durable or otherwise protected from default cleanup.

cleanup.description: Cleanup authority. `never` is the conservative protected default.

max_age.description: Maximum age before an eligible entry may be reclaimed.

max_bytes.description: Maximum aggregate bytes for an eligible entry.

keep_count.description: Minimum number of newest entries to retain.

protect_active.description: Protect entries carrying active process or test-run lease markers.

rationale.description: Human-facing reason this is worth preserving. Optional presentation copy.

storageRootSpec.description: A declarative filesystem root that storage-manager may measure or reclaim.

storageEntry.description: One declared storage surface. The rung describes ownership and relocation capability; budget describes what may be reclaimed.

path.description: Legacy explicit location. Prefer class plus subpath so api-core/storage remains the only path authority.

subpath.description: Optional path below the resolver-selected class root. Must be relative and traversal-safe.

agent_removal.description: Whether a coding agent may delete here: allow, ask (the operator confirms), or deny. Omit to let storage-manager infer it from regenerable and sensitive, which describe backup and reclaim rather than agent permission. See docs/architecture/agent-policy-runtime.md §"Filesystem removal".

regenerable.description: Required deletion intent. true means the owner can reconstruct the entry; false means retention may measure it but must never prune it.

operation.description: Owner API path storage-manager POSTs {"dry_run":false} to when this non-regenerable entry stays over budget. The owner reclaims; storage-manager never deletes non-regenerable data.

ownerCleanupProvider.description: Owner-delegated cleanup provider. Storage Manager discovers this declaration and delegates Estimate, Preview, and Apply to the declaring scenario; it never opens owner-private storage.

storage_entries.description: Storage entry names this provider is authorized to manage. A self-approving owner budget is valid only when one of these entries is regenerable and budgeted.

cleanup_providers.description: Cleanup surfaces implemented by this owner and callable through Storage Manager's owner-delegation protocol.

rationale.description: Why the owner has these storage entries, or why an explicit empty declaration is accurate.

retentionBudget.description: One declared storage ceiling the framework enforces. Consumed by packages/api-core/retention, which prunes the target down to whichever bound binds first and reports which one it was. NOT a backup declaration: durable_data answers 'preserve this' and its `regenerable: false` means never delete, while a retention budget answers 'this may never exceed this much'. A budget must declare at least one bound; an age bound alone is a promise proportional to an ingest rate the scenario usually does not control, so it is accepted but reported as unbounded in size.

target.description: What this budget bounds. Paths are relative to the scenario's own storage-class root and resolve through api-core/storage, so a shadow variant prunes its own data and never live's.

kind.description: sqlite_table bounds rows in one table of one SQLite database; directory bounds the top-level entries of one directory; file bounds one regenerable file.

class.description: Storage class root the target path is relative to (api-core/storage Class). Defaults to data.

database.description: sqlite_table only. Slash-normalized path of the SQLite database, relative to the class root (e.g. autoheal.sqlite).

table.description: sqlite_table only. Table the budget bounds.

time_column.description: sqlite_table only. Column carrying the row's age, used to order deletes oldest-first and to evaluate max_age.

path.description: directory only. Slash-normalized directory path relative to the class root.

max_age.description: Age bound with an explicit unit, hours or days (e.g. 30d, 72h). An age bound alone is not a size bound.

max_bytes.description: Size bound with an explicit unit (e.g. 2GiB). A unit is mandatory: a bare integer invites a 1000x mistake that is invisible in review and is a disk outage.

pruner.description: builtin uses the framework pruner for the target kind and needs no scenario Go code. custom requires the scenario to register a retention.Pruner under this budget's key; the framework still owns whether the target is within budget, the scenario owns which rows die.

rationale.description: Why this ceiling, and what drives the volume. Read by whoever next has to decide whether the number is still right.

retention.description: Declared storage ceilings for the data this component accumulates, enforced by packages/api-core/retention without per-component code. Distinct from durable_data, which declares what to back up.

budgets.description: Budgets keyed by stable logical name. The key names the budget in findings and logs, and is the registry name a custom pruner registers under.

deploymentSupportedTarget.description: One target platform the component declares it can be deployed to. The closure resolver refuses platforms outside this list with a typed unsupported_platform entry; an absent list defers to resource artifacts.

distribution.description: Optional distribution the claim was evidenced on, e.g. ubuntu.

version.description: Optional distribution version the claim was evidenced on, e.g. 24.04.

deploymentPersistentData.description: One persistent data set a deployment must preserve across updates and restores. It names the owner (the component whose lifecycle holds the data), the binding the owner uses to reach it, the backup provider, and who owns schema migration. The closure carries these so the manifest can identify the recovery contract of every data set.

owner.description: Component id that owns the data (a resource such as postgres, or the declaring scenario). Defaults to the declaring component.

binding.description: Declared binding the owner uses to locate the data, e.g. schema:<name>, data-dir, bucket:<name>. Never a host path.

backup_provider.description: Declared provider reference that captures this data set (e.g. data-backup-manager).

migration_owner.description: Who applies schema/data migrations when the code revision changes.

deploymentListener.description: Edge exposure and readiness for one declared port. Ports not listed here are private to the target.

port.description: Key of the ports map this listener refers to.

visibility.description: public_via_edge: reachable through the deployment edge (reverse proxy/TLS); private: bound to the target only.

path_prefix.description: Optional path prefix on the public host. Empty means the listener is the host fallback.

readiness.description: Readiness probe the edge waits on before routing. Defaults to the owning component's run.readiness.

deploymentRecovery.description: Recovery contract for code and schema. It tells the planner which rollbacks are safe without the operator reading the scenario's source.

code_rollback.description: Which earlier releases the code can be rolled back to while the current data remains in place.

schema_strategy.description: expand_contract: migrations are backward compatible for one release; explicit_restore: rollback requires restoring a backup; none: no schema.

deploymentDeclaration.description: Additive deployment declarations read by the scenario-to-cloud closure resolver. Declared facts only; deployability verdicts are derived and never stored here.

credentialDescriptor.description: Declares one credential by a durable, backend-neutral name. logical_id and field are the only identifiers the credential store ever sees; a descriptor never names Vault, a file, or any other provider-shaped path. Replaces the retired secretDescriptor.

logical_id.description: Stable namespaced identity, e.g. vrooli/openrouter. Durable across hosts, platforms, and deployment tiers.

field.description: Which value of that identity this descriptor addresses, e.g. api-key. Defaults to 'value'.

env.description: Process environment variable to inject the value into. Optional, and declared ONLY when the consumer is a process Vrooli does not author — a database container, a third-party CLI — which can receive a value no other way. Vrooli-authored code omits this and resolves through the credential-authority binding for its language, which keeps the value out of the process environment where it would be readable at /proc/<pid>/environ and inherited by every subprocess.

required.description: Whether the declaring component can do its job without this value. A missing application credential never blocks a start; it makes the component report unhealthy.

label.description: Human-readable display name shown in onboarding and admin surfaces.

description.description: Why this credential is needed and what it unlocks.

placeholder.description: Safe, non-secret sample text shown inside an operator input. It communicates the expected shape and must never be a usable credential value.

obtain_url.description: Where an operator signs up for or generates this credential.

provisioning.description: Who supplies this value. operator: a person provides it. derived: the declaring component writes it once derived_from is present. generated: the declaring component mints it out of nothing, typically on first start, because there is nowhere an operator could obtain it. Only an operator-supplied value may block configuration while it is absent.

derived_from.description: Field that must be present before a derived credential can be provisioned.

tiers.description: Deployment tiers where this credential is required. Empty or omitted means every tier.

owner.description: Owner that supplies the registered setup and verification actions.

version.description: Versioned operator-capability descriptor contract. Unknown versions are rejected by the control plane.

credentials.description: The credentials block shared by resource manifests and scenario service manifests. Both use one shape on purpose: a scenario-declared credential and a resource-declared one must be the same thing to the store, the diagnosis, and the recovery bundle. A credential nothing declares is a credential no backup captures.

deploymentBackupArgv.description: One declared backup/restore/quiesce hook as {tool, argv[]}. Credentials never travel in argv; the caller supplies them through the child environment.

tool.description: Executable name (resolved on PATH or beneath the owner's native binary directory). Never a shell string.

argv.description: Arguments. Whole-argument placeholders {database}, {output}, {input} are substituted by the caller; a placeholder is never split into extra arguments.

deploymentBackupHook.description: Declared consistency boundary and backup tooling for the component's persistent data. A resource that owns a database declares its database-native dump/restore argv here (a generic file copy of a live database is never a backup); a scenario declares the quiesce/release hooks that coordinate writes across its data stores. Read by scenario-to-cloud recovery points and by the target-local `vrooli cloud-target data` verbs.

provider.description: Which recovery-point provider captures this component's bindings.
